title: Strict henselization commutes with surjective local quotients
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative local ring, $K$ a separable closure of its residue field, with compatible $A$-algebra and residue-field algebra structures. Let $C$ be an $A$-algebra and assume that $C$ is an algebraic strict henselization of $A$ relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Let $B$ be a commutative local ring and $\pi:A\to B$ a surjective ring homomorphism with kernel $I\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$. There exist a field $L$ which is a separable closure of the residue field of $B$, compatible residue-field and $B$-algebra structures on $L$, and a $B$-algebra structure on the explicit quotient $C/IC$, where $IC$ is extension under $A\to C$, such that $C/IC$ is an algebraic strict henselization of $B$ relative to $L$.

source.place: Tag 05WS, algebra.tex, lemma-quotient-strict-henselization. The pointed-etale finality argument is written by U2 for the project colimit definition.

proof.text: Identify B with A/I by the first isomorphism theorem. Its residue field is canonically that of A, so transport the given separable closure and let its B-action factor through the residue field.

Base change of pointed etale A-algebras to B is final. For a pointed etale B-algebra S choose a standard etale principal neighbourhood at its distinguished prime and lift its coefficients and inverted Jacobian determinant to A; this provides an arrow S to a base-changed object. For two such arrows take the tensor product of their lifted A-algebras with its induced point in K. The two resulting maps from S agree at that point. The diagonal of an etale algebra is open, so a principal neighbourhood equalizes them; lift its denominator and invert it in the A-tensor product. This proves the comma category nonempty and connected.

Extension of scalars is left adjoint and preserves the universal cocone giving C. Its new vertex B tensor_A C is the explicit quotient C/IC. Finality identifies this with the universal pointed etale B-algebra cocone. This is exactly the predicate IsStrictHenselization, with the B-map obtained from the explicit quotient construction.

theorem IsStrictHenselization.surjective_quotient
    (A K C B : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [Field K]
    [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) K] [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) K]
    [Algebra A K] [IsScalarTower A (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A) K]
    [CommRing C] [Algebra A C] (hC : IsStrictHenselization A K C)
    [CommRing B] [IsLocalRing B]
    (π : A →+* B) (hπ : Function.Surjective π)
    (I : Ideal A) (hI : I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A) (hker : RingHom.ker π = I) :
    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L)
      (_ : Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) L)
      (_ : IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) L)
      (_ : Algebra B L) (_ : IsScalarTower B (IsLocalRing.ResidueField B) L)
      (_ : Algebra B (C ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A C))),
      IsStrictHenselization B L (C ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A C))
